title: I asked Codex for a game where I could “just wander around and be afraid of something.” Here are the prompts and token counts for v0.1.0
author: Gorgogon
selftext:
My English isn’t great, so I used Codex to translate this post. If I’d written it in English myself, you’d have had to untangle some awkward sentences and guess which tense I meant. I wanted it to be easy to read.

I built *The Lower Vaults*, a first-person exploration game in Godot, over roughly four hours one evening. You start on a wooden bridge between walls of archive drawers. From there, stairways lead to tidal cisterns, observatories, and forests of tuning forks. Something can follow you, and you can hear it before you see it.

At least, that was the idea. In my first playtest, my footsteps drowned out everything else, I kept ending up in the machine room, and the impossible architecture had a perfectly ordinary floor. Most of my follow-up prompts came from playing each build and trying to explain what felt off.

# The numbers

|Tool|Sessions|Tokens|
|:-|:-|:-|
|Codex|4 main sessions and 6 subagent sessions|75,875,836|
|Claude Code|1 session for GitHub and release work|1,645,162|
|**Total**|**11 sessions**|**77,520,998**|

**98.45% of those tokens were cached input.** Excluding cache reads, the total was **1,199,332 tokens**, including **364,313 tokens of model output**. These figures come from the local session logs and exclude the session where I asked for the count.

# The prompts that shaped v0.1.0

These are the main prompts in order. I’ve grouped a few consecutive messages and skipped the repeated “launch it again” and “commit this” requests.

**The original idea**

>You have Godot and Blender. I want to explore endless dimensions in a game, like Escher’s worlds or Piranesi’s architecture. I just want to wander around and be afraid of something.  
>  
>Use multiple agents!

**After the first playtest**

>The transitions don’t feel seamless. The worlds don’t feel different. There’s no tension or suspense. I want that feeling without getting killed.

>My footsteps are so loud they drown out the rest of the sound. I keep getting the machine room. I want more lighting effects and shadows. Use fewer light sources and make it darker and gloomier. Give me at least 30 different scenes and at least 10 different characters that put me on edge. Use multiple agents.

**Getting the pursuer right**

>All the entry points are on the same horizontal plane. I wanted non-Euclidean spaces. The graphics lack detail and everything looks too soft and plush.  
>  
>The pursuer should only back off and disappear once I’ve looked at it for more than five seconds or I’m more than 20 meters away. Only one pursuer at a time. It should find a path to me instead of walking into walls. Spawn it at least five meters away from me.

**Explaining what I meant by impossible architecture**

>What I mean by non-Euclidean space is that there’s no fixed up, down, or sideways. A path can run along any axis.

>I like the way the space bends, but I want it to work like *Antichamber*. It shouldn’t be obvious where a path will take me. The spaces should use all three dimensions. Right now you never get, say, three different settings stacked on top of each other.

>Commit this, then use subagents to work through every setting. Give each one stairways that lead to other levels as well as those smooth transitions. By the way, keep the well.

**Getting the build out**

>Make the game multilingual, prepare Linux and Windows builds, and write a README. Use the ten most popular languages. Check the language list with me first.

>Make English the main README, put links to the other languages alongside it, and include screenshots.

The prompt I’d use again is “three different settings stacked on top of each other.” I’d said “non-Euclidean” several times. Once I described something I expected to see, I had a way to judge the next build. Could I stand on a staircase, look down the well, and see somewhere else I could actually walk to?

The Linux and Windows builds are on GitHub. If you try it, I’d love to hear where you first lost your bearings. [The Lower Vaults on GitHub](https://github.com/ArcheeNic/lower-vaults)
